I will keep things simple and steady this year. In Quzhou, the land and water conditions fit the usual wheat and summer maize rotation best, and at my age I care first about reliable harvest, easy machine work, and not taking big market risk. So I will put most of my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. That gives me two harvests from one piece of land, the buyers are easy to find, and I already know how to manage it. I will use improved seed rather than old saved seed because I want more even emergence and less trouble. I will fertilize moderately, not too heavily, because too much fertilizer costs money and can make lodging or waste. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat here depends more on timely water, especially at jointing and grain filling. I will spray only when needed, mainly for common weeds, aphids, and diseases, because I want to control cost. On a small piece of land I will plant peanuts in summer to spread risk a little, improve the soil a bit, and keep some cash flexibility, but I will not make peanuts my main crop because wheat and maize are still safer for me.
